#!/usr/bin/env bash
# teardown.sh - remove a preview environment's cloud resources.
#
#   ./teardown.sh <env> [--dry-run]
#
# <env> is a preview env from conf/previews.conf (e.g. pr-482). Resources are
# found with the env's label selector and deleted through cloudctl.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/inventory.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/inventory.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/order.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/order.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/report.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/report.sh"

usage() {
    echo "usage: $0 <env> [--dry-run]" >&2
    exit 2
}

[[ $# -ge 1 ]] || usage
ENV_ARG="$1"; shift
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
        *) usage ;;
    esac
done

load_env_config "$ENV_ARG"
echo "teardown: env=$ENV_NAME project=$ENV_PROJECT selector=$ENV_SELECTOR"

inventory="$(inventory_collect "$ENV_SELECTOR")"
echo "teardown: $(printf '%s\n' "$inventory" | grep -c . || true) resource(s) found"

# TODO(PLAT-311): volumes have to be detached before they can be deleted.
# TODO(PLAT-311): make re-runs safe and write the report (lib/report.sh).
printf '%s\n' "$inventory" | order_resources | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id kind name; do
    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "would delete $kind $id ($name)"
        continue
    fi
    echo "deleting $kind $id ($name)"
    "$CLOUDCTL" delete "$id"
done

echo "teardown: done"

# shellcheck shell=bash
# Teardown report: one markdown file per env under $REPORT_DIR.
#
#   report_init ENV           start a new report (truncates the scratch rows)
#   report_add ACTION ID KIND NAME [NOTE]
#   report_write              render reports/<env>.md, prints its path

REPORT_DIR="${REPORT_DIR:-$ROOT/reports}"
_REPORT_ENV=""
_REPORT_ROWS=""

report_init() {
    _REPORT_ENV="$1"
    mkdir -p "$REPORT_DIR"
    _REPORT_ROWS="$(mktemp)"
}

report_add() {
    [[ -n "$_REPORT_ROWS" ]] || { echo "report: report_init not called" >&2; return 1; }
    local action="$1" id="$2" kind="$3" name="$4" note="${5:-}"
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$action" "$id" "$kind" "$name" "$note" >> "$_REPORT_ROWS"
}

report_path() {
    echo "$REPORT_DIR/${_REPORT_ENV}.md"
}

report_write() {
    local out action id kind name note
    out="$(report_path)"
    {
        echo "# Teardown report: ${_REPORT_ENV}"
        echo
        echo "- generated: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
        echo "- selector: ${ENV_SELECTOR:-?}"
        echo
        if [[ ! -s "$_REPORT_ROWS" ]]; then
            echo "Nothing to do: no resources matched."
        else
            echo "| action | id | kind | name | note |"
            echo "|---|---|---|---|---|"
            while IFS=$'\t' read -r action id kind name note; do
                echo "| $action | $id | $kind | $name | $note |"
            done < "$_REPORT_ROWS"
        fi
    } > "$out"
    rm -f "$_REPORT_ROWS"
    echo "$out"
}

# shellcheck shell=bash
# Inventory helpers: map a preview env to its label selector and list what it owns.
#
# Environment overrides:
#   CLOUDCTL        cloudctl binary to call (default: cloudctl on PATH)
#   PREVIEWS_CONF   env -> selector mapping (default: conf/previews.conf)

CLOUDCTL="${CLOUDCTL:-cloudctl}"
PREVIEWS_CONF="${PREVIEWS_CONF:-$ROOT/conf/previews.conf}"

# load_env_config ENV
# Sets ENV_NAME, ENV_PROJECT and ENV_SELECTOR from the config file.
load_env_config() {
    local want="$1" env project selector
    [[ -r "$PREVIEWS_CONF" ]] || { echo "inventory: cannot read $PREVIEWS_CONF" >&2; return 1; }
    while read -r env project selector _; do
        [[ -z "$env" || "$env" == \#* ]] && continue
        if [[ "$env" == "$want" ]]; then
            ENV_NAME="$env"
            ENV_PROJECT="$project"
            ENV_SELECTOR="$selector"
            return 0
        fi
    done < "$PREVIEWS_CONF"
    echo "inventory: unknown preview env '$want' (see $PREVIEWS_CONF)" >&2
    return 1
}

# inventory_collect SELECTOR
# Prints one line per resource: "<id>\t<kind>\t<name>".
inventory_collect() {
    local selector="$1"
    "$CLOUDCTL" list --selector "$selector" --json \
        | jq -r '.[] | [.id, .kind, .name] | @tsv'
}

# inventory_json ID
# Full JSON description of one resource (includes "dependents": [ids]).
inventory_json() {
    "$CLOUDCTL" describe "$1" --json
}

# inventory_field ID FIELD
# Prints one top-level field of a resource ("" when unset).
inventory_field() {
    inventory_json "$1" | jq -r --arg f "$2" '.[$f] // empty'
}

# inventory_exists ID -> 0 if the resource is still there
inventory_exists() {
    "$CLOUDCTL" describe "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}
# shellcheck shell=bash
# Ordering of resources for teardown.
#
# Resources have to go in reverse dependency order: cloudctl refuses to delete
# anything that still has dependents (see `cloudctl --help`).

# order_rank KIND -> numeric rank; lower ranks are processed first.
# NOTE: copied from the provisioning side (create order) -- still needs to be
# turned into a teardown order and to cover every kind we provision.
order_rank() {
    case "$1" in
        network)  echo 10 ;;
        subnet)   echo 20 ;;
        instance) echo 30 ;;
        *)        echo 99 ;;
    esac
}

# order_resources < "<id>\t<kind>\t<name>" lines
# Prints the same lines sorted by rank (stable within a rank).

    while IFS=$'\t' read -r id kind name; do

        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(order_rank "$kind")" "$id" "$kind" "$name"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# teardown.sh - remove a preview environment's cloud resources.
#
#   ./teardown.sh <env> [--dry-run]
#
# <env> is a preview env from conf/previews.conf (e.g. pr-482). Resources are
# found with the env's label selector and deleted through cloudctl.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/inventory.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/inventory.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/order.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/order.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/report.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/report.sh"

usage() {
    echo "usage: $0 <env> [--dry-run]" >&2
    exit 2
}

[[ $# -ge 1 ]] || usage
ENV_ARG="$1"; shift
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
        *) usage ;;
    esac
done

load_env_config "$ENV_ARG"
echo "teardown: env=$ENV_NAME project=$ENV_PROJECT selector=$ENV_SELECTOR"

inventory="$(inventory_collect "$ENV_SELECTOR")"
echo "teardown: $(printf '%s\n' "$inventory" | grep -c . || true) resource(s) found"

# Keep an existing deletion report on an empty rerun, rather than replacing
# the audit trail with an empty report. An initially empty env still gets one.
if [[ -z "$inventory" ]]; then
    echo "teardown: nothing to do (no resources matched)"
    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]]; then
        if [[ ! -f "$REPORT_DIR/${ENV_NAME}.md" ]]; then
            report_init "$ENV_NAME"
            report_write
        else
            echo "teardown: report retained: $REPORT_DIR/${ENV_NAME}.md"
        fi
    fi
    exit 0
fi

ordered_inventory="$(printf '%s\n' "$inventory" | order_resources)"

if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]]; then
    report_init "$ENV_NAME"
    # Write successful actions even if a later dependency or API error stops us.
    # Do not let report generation hide the original failure status.
    finish_report() {
        local status=$?
        trap - EXIT
        report_write || { [[ "$status" -ne 0 ]] || status=1; }
        exit "$status"
    }
    trap finish_report EXIT
fi

# Use a redirected loop, not a pipeline subshell, so failures reach the EXIT
# trap and reporting remains in the main shell. Never cascade outside selector.
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id kind name; do
    if [[ "$kind" == "volume" ]]; then
        attached_to="$(inventory_field "$id" attached_to)"
        if [[ -n "$attached_to" ]]; then
            if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
                echo "would detach volume $id ($name) from $attached_to"
            else
                echo "detaching volume $id ($name) from $attached_to"
                "$CLOUDCTL" volume detach "$id"
                report_add detached "$id" "$kind" "$name" "from $attached_to"
            fi
        fi
    fi
    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "would delete $kind $id ($name)"
        continue
    fi
    echo "deleting $kind $id ($name)"
    "$CLOUDCTL" delete "$id"
    report_add deleted "$id" "$kind" "$name"
done <<< "$ordered_inventory"

echo "teardown: done"
# shellcheck shell=bash
# Ordering of resources for teardown.
#
# Resources have to go in reverse dependency order: cloudctl refuses to delete
# anything that still has dependents (see `cloudctl --help`).

# order_rank KIND -> numeric rank; lower ranks are processed first.
order_rank() {
    case "$1" in
        dns)      echo 10 ;;
        lb)       echo 20 ;;
        volume)   echo 30 ;;
        instance) echo 40 ;;
        subnet)   echo 50 ;;
        network)  echo 60 ;;
        *)        echo 99 ;;
    esac
}

# order_resources < "<id>\t<kind>\t<name>" lines
# Prints the same lines sorted by rank (stable within a rank).
order_resources() {
    local id kind name
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r id kind name; do
        [[ -z "$id" ]] && continue
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(order_rank "$kind")" "$id" "$kind" "$name"
    done | sort -s -n -k1,1 | cut -f2-
}
